    For R users: the layer contract

    r-users.Rmd

    Under every input format sits one internal currency: the qm_layer — an sf object in long format (one row per site per time step) carrying its metadata as attributes. The from_*() wrappers all produce one; this page is the contract for building and inspecting them directly.

    1. Canonical columns

    Column Type Meaning
    code character stable site id, links a symbol across time steps
    time_label character display text per step (absent = static layer)
    time_sort POSIXct sort key parsed from the label
    value column numeric/character the mapped values, named by value_col
    lat, lon numeric WGS84
    geometry sfc the sf geometry (built from lat/lon if absent)

    Legacy names are accepted and normalised: siteCode→code, year_str→time_label, Latitude/Longitude→lat/lon.

    2. Construction and inspection 

    library(quickmap)
d <- data.frame(
  code = rep(c("A", "B"), each = 3),
  date = rep(as.Date(c("2024-01-01", "2024-02-01", "2024-03-01")), 2),
  no2  = c(31, 28, 25, 44, 41, 37),
  lat  = rep(c(51.44, 51.46), each = 3),
  lon  = rep(c(-0.17, -0.21), each = 3)
)
layer <- qm_layer(d, name = "survey")      # infers value, time, resolution
qm_meta(layer)                             # value_col, time_col, shape, ...
print(layer)                               # "2 sites x 3 time steps [month]"

    Explicit overrides: value_col, time_col (pass it for non-date orderings like diurnal hours), label_col, shape, name.

    3. The time grammar

    time_label values must all share one format; the format sets the animation’s resolution:

    Format Resolution
    YYYY year
    YYYY-MM month
    YYYY-MM-DD day
    YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM(:SS) hour/minute

    Date/POSIXct columns are recognised by class wherever they appear; character columns are only parsed if named date, time, datetime, time_label or year_str — a gate-named column that fails the grammar is a loud error, never a silent guess.

    4. Inference, in order

    When not told explicitly, qm_layer() infers:

    • value column: a known pollutant name (no2, pm25, pm10, nox, o3, …), else the single remaining candidate column — two candidates is an error asking for value_col.
    • time column: by class, then by the name gate above; none = a static layer.
    • labels: a Label or School column if present.
    • shape: none — the map assigns symbols (solid for temporal layers, outline for static, in layer order) unless the layer or the map-level data_symbols says otherwise.

    5. The compatibility wrapper

    create_pollution_map() is the historic entry point, kept working with its original signature; it converts data_sources to qm_layers and delegates to quickmap(). New code should call quickmap(); old scripts need no changes.
